meta.titre: Consumer Behaviour: utility, choice and the budget
meta.sous_theme: Utility, diminishing marginal utility, consumer equilibrium and types of goods

sections.contenu_markdown: A student in Bamenda has 1,000 FCFA to spend on a snack, phone credit and a notebook. Whatever she chooses, she gives up the others, so she tries to get the most satisfaction from limited money. The first plate of food after a long school day is delightful; the fourth hardly adds anything. Economists turn this common experience into rules about utility and choice. GCE papers ask for definitions such as utility, tables of total and marginal utility with missing values, and the difference between normal and inferior goods.

items: Scarcity means that wants are unlimited while the resources to satisfy them are limited.
Demand is the quantity of a good that buyers are willing and able to buy at a given price.
A household's income limits what it can buy.
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up.

sections.titre: Utility, diminishing marginal utility and consumer choice
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Utility

**Utility** is the satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming a good or service. It is not the same as usefulness: a drink may give more utility than a useful tool. Economists use imaginary units called **utils** to compare satisfaction.

- **Total utility (TU)**: the satisfaction from all the units consumed.
- **Marginal utility (MU)**: the extra satisfaction from consuming one more unit.

$$MU_n = TU_n - TU_{n-1} \qquad TU_n = TU_{n-1} + MU_n$$

For the first unit, $MU = TU$.

### Law of diminishing marginal utility

As a consumer takes more units of a good in a given time, the marginal utility of each extra unit eventually falls, if tastes do not change. Total utility keeps rising while marginal utility is positive, is greatest when marginal utility is zero, and falls if marginal utility becomes negative.

| Units | MU | TU |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 70 | 70 |
| 2 | 50 | 120 |
| 3 | 30 | 150 |
| 4 | 10 | 160 |
| 5 | -10 | 150 |

### Consumer equilibrium

A consumer with a fixed budget gets the most total utility when the last franc spent on each good gives the same extra utility, and the whole budget is spent:

$$\frac{MU_A}{P_A} = \frac{MU_B}{P_B}$$

If $\frac{MU_A}{P_A}$ is greater, moving money from B to A raises total utility.

### Consumer sovereignty

Consumers decide, through what they choose to buy, which goods firms produce. Firms that fail to satisfy buyers lose sales. The idea is limited by advertising, monopoly and government rules.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a table has missing values of TU or MU
variantes.contenu_markdown: Find a missing MU by subtracting the TU of the previous row from the TU of the same row. Find a missing TU by adding the MU to the TU of the previous row. The first row has $TU = MU$. Check that MU falls down the table.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question links demand to income
variantes.contenu_markdown: A **normal good** is one whose demand rises as income rises. An **inferior good** is one whose demand falls as income rises, because buyers switch to better goods; the word does not mean poor quality. A **luxury good** is a normal good whose demand rises faster than income.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When a question asks why consumers buy different amounts
variantes.contenu_markdown: Besides income, buying decisions depend on the **price** of the good, the prices of **substitutes** and **complements**, **tastes** and fashion, advertising, expectations about future prices, and credit available.

sections.enonce_markdown:
A consumer has a budget of 400 FCFA to spend on goods X and Y. Good X costs 100 FCFA per unit and good Y costs 50 FCFA per unit. The marginal utility of each successive unit is:

| Unit | MU of X (utils) | MU of Y (utils) |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 200 | 120 |
| 2nd | 120 | 100 |
| 3rd | 80 | 80 |
| 4th | 40 | 60 |
| 5th | - | 40 |

(a) Calculate the marginal utility per franc for each unit.

(b) Find the combination of X and Y that gives the greatest satisfaction for the budget.

(c) State the total utility obtained.

etapes.action: Divide each MU by its price.
etapes.justification: A franc should go where it adds the most utility.

etapes.action: Rank the units from the highest MU per franc.
etapes.justification: The consumer buys the best-value unit first.

etapes.action: Buy in this order while watching the budget.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Y1 50, X1 150, Y2 200, Y3 250, X2 350, Y4 400. The budget is used up.

etapes.justification: In equilibrium the last franc must earn the same on each good.
etapes.resultat_markdown: X: 2 units, MU per franc of the 2nd unit $= \frac{120}{100} = 1.2$. Y: 4 units, MU per franc of the 4th unit $= \frac{60}{50} = 1.2$. Equal.

etapes.action: Add the utilities of the units bought.
etapes.justification: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The consumer buys **2 units of X and 4 units of Y**, spending 200 + 200 = 400 FCFA, and obtains a total utility of **680 utils**. No other affordable combination gives more.

items.erreur_markdown: "Marginal utility is falling, so total utility is falling."
items.pourquoi_faux: Total utility keeps rising as long as each extra unit still adds some satisfaction, even a smaller amount.
items.correction_markdown: TU rises while MU is positive, is at its maximum when MU is zero and falls only when MU is negative.

items.erreur_markdown: "Marginal utility is the satisfaction from all the units consumed."
items.pourquoi_faux: That is total utility. Marginal utility refers only to the additional unit.

items.erreur_markdown: "An inferior good is a good of bad quality."
items.pourquoi_faux: The word describes how demand reacts to income, not the quality of the good.
items.correction_markdown: An inferior good is one whose demand falls when income rises.

items.erreur_markdown: "Consumer sovereignty means that consumers fix the prices of goods."
items.pourquoi_faux: The idea concerns what is produced, not who sets prices.
items.correction_markdown: Consumers' spending decides which goods firms produce.

items.erreur_markdown: "The consumer should buy the good with the highest marginal utility."
items.pourquoi_faux: A good with high utility may be very dear. Utility must be compared per franc spent.
items.correction_markdown: Compare $\frac{MU}{P}$ for each good and spend until the ratios are equal.

items.enonce_markdown:
The table shows the satisfaction a consumer gets from bags of groundnuts.

| Bags | MU (utils) | TU (utils) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 90 | |
| 2 | 70 | 160 |
| 3 | | 200 |
| 4 | 20 | |
| 5 | | 210 |

(a) Complete the table.

(b) At how many bags is total utility greatest?

(c) Name the law shown by the table.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) $TU_1 = MU_1 = 90$. $MU_3 = 200 - 160 = 40$. $TU_4 = 200 + 20 = 220$. $MU_5 = 210 - 220 = -10$. The completed values are **90, 40, 220 and -10**.

(b) Total utility is greatest at **4 bags** (220 utils); the 5th bag lowers it.

(c) The **law of diminishing marginal utility**: each extra bag adds less than the one before.

items.enonce_markdown:
When a household's monthly income rises from 60,000 FCFA to 100,000 FCFA, its weekly purchases change as follows: good P from 10 kg to 6 kg and good Q from 5 kg to 9 kg.

(a) Classify P and Q as normal or inferior goods.

(b) Calculate the percentage change in income and in the quantity of Q.

(c) Say whether Q behaves like a luxury good.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Demand for P falls while income rises: P is an **inferior good**. Demand for Q rises with income: Q is a **normal good**.

(b) Income: $\frac{100000 - 60000}{60000} \times 100 \approx$ **66.7%**. Quantity of Q: $\frac{9 - 5}{5} \times 100 =$ **80%**.

(c) The quantity of Q rises by 80%, faster than income at 66.7%, so Q behaves like a **luxury good**.

items.enonce_markdown:
A consumer has 200 FCFA. Good A costs 40 FCFA a unit and good B costs 20 FCFA a unit. Marginal utilities in utils:

| Unit | MU of A | MU of B |
|---|---|---|
| 1st | 80 | 50 |
| 2nd | 60 | 40 |
| 3rd | 40 | 30 |
| 4th | 20 | 20 |
| 5th | - | 10 |

(a) Find the combination that maximises total utility and state the total utility.

(b) Show that buying 4 units of A and 2 units of B, which also costs 200 FCFA, is worse.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) MU per franc: A: 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.5; B: 2.5, 2.0, 1.5, 1.0, 0.5. Buy in order: B1 (20), A1 (60), B2 (80), A2 (120), B3 (140), then A3 and B4 both give 1.0: A3 (180), B4 (200). The consumer buys **3 units of A and 4 units of B**, costing 120 + 80 = 200 FCFA. Both last units give 1.0 util per franc. Total utility $= (80 + 60 + 40) + (50 + 40 + 30 + 20) = 180 + 140 =$ **320 utils**.

(b) 4 A and 2 B costs 160 + 40 = 200 FCFA. Total utility $= (80 + 60 + 40 + 20) + (50 + 40) = 200 + 90 =$ **290 utils**, which is less than 320. The 4th unit of A gives only 0.5 util per franc, while the 3rd and 4th units of B give 1.5 and 1.0.

items_markdown: Utility is satisfaction; total utility is the sum of the satisfaction from all units, and marginal utility is the addition from the last unit.
Marginal utility eventually falls as more units are consumed; total utility is at its highest when marginal utility is zero.
A consumer with a budget is in equilibrium when $\frac{MU}{P}$ is equal for every good and all the money is spent.
A normal good has demand rising with income; an inferior good has demand falling with income.
Consumer sovereignty means consumers' spending directs what firms produce.
